title: Rigveda 5.20: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.20: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.20 is a hymn of 4 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 334v-335r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.20.1-3 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 1, varga 12); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 334v
translation.original_text:
1yam a̍gne vājasātama̱ tvaṁ ci̱n manya̍se ra̱yim | taṁ no̍ gī̱rbhiḥ śra̱vāyya̍ṁ deva̱trā pa̍nayā̱ yuja̍m ||
2ye a̍gne̱ neraya̍nti te vṛ̱ddhā u̱grasya̱ śava̍saḥ | apa̱ dveṣo̱ apa̱ hvaro̱ 'nyavra̍tasya saścire ||
3hotā̍raṁ tvā vṛṇīma̱he 'gne̱ dakṣa̍sya̱ sādha̍nam | ya̱jñeṣu̍ pū̱rvyaṁ gi̱rā praya̍svanto havāmahe ||
translation.text:
1AGNI, best winner of the spoil, cause us to praise before the Gods As our associate meet for lauds, wealth which thou verily deemest wealth.
2Agni, the great who ward not off the anger of thy power and might Stir up the wrath and hatred due to one who holds an alien creed.
3Thee, Agni, would we choose as Priest, the perfecter of strength and skill; We who bring sacred food invoke with song thee Chief at holy rites.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 334v (numbered 7v by the scribe) (OPenn image 335, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.19.4 ‹-priyam dugdham na kāmyam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 335r (numbered 8r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.20.4 ‹-yathā te ūtaye sahasāvan›. Verses 5.20.1-3 end on this page.

1yam | agne | vāja-sātama | tvam | cit | manyase | rayim | tam | naḥ | gīḥ-bhiḥ | śravāyyam | deva-trā | panaya | yujam
2ye | agne | na | īrayanti | te | vṛddhāḥ | ugrasya | śavasaḥ | apa | dveṣaḥ | apa | hvaraḥ | anya-vratasya | saścire
3hotāram | tvā | vṛṇīmahe | agne | dakṣasya | sādhanam | yajñeṣu | pūrvyam | girā | prayasvantaḥ | havāmahe

translation.original_ref: RV 5.20.4 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 1, varga 12); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 335r
translation.original_text: <sup>4</sup>i̱tthā yathā̍ ta ū̱taye̱ saha̍sāvan di̱ve-di̍ve | rā̱ya ṛ̱tāya̍ sukrato̱ gobhi̍ḥ ṣyāma sadha̱mādo̍ vī̱raiḥ syā̍ma sadha̱māda̍ḥ ||
translation.text: <sup>4</sup>Here as is needful for thine aid we toil, O Conqueror, day by day, For wealth, for Law. May we rejoice, Most Wise One! at the feast, with kine, rejoice, with heroes, at the feast.
